transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's good to meet you too. 

I, um, I came in because I’ve started doing things that honestly kind of scare me. Like, I'll just walk out in the middle of major system deployments at work, or I'll go driving around late at night with absolutely no plan. And... well, that is just not how I’ve ever handled stress before. So I figured I needed to talk to someone.
During these times, have you been feeling unusually high or unusually irritable?
No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel high or overly irritable. It's more like... I just feel overwhelmed, and I have to get away from whatever is happening. I just feel this need to escape.
When you suddenly leave like that, is it usually after you feel like someone might reject you or leave you?

No, I don't think so. It's... it's not really about other people, like worrying they're going to reject me or leave. It doesn't feel connected to that at all. It's more just... hitting a wall and needing to get out of wherever I am right then.
Did these urges to suddenly leave start after a specific stressful event happened in your life?

Yes, actually. Um, this all started after a specific incident at work. It was a late-night cutover... a major system migration that went really wrong. That was a little over a year ago, I'd say about 13 months now. Ever since then, I've had these urges.
Since that work incident, have you had unwanted memories of it that suddenly pop into your mind?

Yes, I have. They really just come out of nowhere. Um, especially if I'm in that conference area at work, or if someone just raises their voice on a call... I'll suddenly get hit with images and sounds from that night. It comes on so strongly that I completely lose track of what I was even saying.
Since that incident, have you been avoiding reminders of what happened?

Yes, definitely. I actually take the long way around the building now just to stay away from that area, and I avoid that whole floor whenever I can. And if people bring it up... like, the moment anyone starts talking about the contractor or the cutover, I just shut the conversation down right away. I really don't want to be around anything that reminds me of it.
Since that incident, have you been feeling constantly on guard or watchful, like something bad might happen?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't really walk around feeling on edge or like I'm waiting for another disaster to happen. As long as I can just avoid those reminders we talked about, I generally feel okay in that regard. I haven't really noticed being constantly watchful.
Have you had nightmares about what happened during that work incident?

Yes, I have. Most nights I just lie there replaying pieces of the office incident in my head. Then, um, when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I wake up really tense—either from dreams about it or just from some small noise. I end up being completely exhausted before work even starts.
During that work incident, did you think that you or someone else might die or be seriously injured?

No, I didn't. I mean, it was incredibly stressful and chaotic, but I never thought anyone was in physical danger or going to die or anything like that. It was just a really bad situation at work, not a life-or-death kind of thing.
Have these symptoms been interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Yes, it really has been. Um, I just had my performance review, and it was the first time I've ever been told that I'm missing key handoffs. They said I've been leaving meetings abruptly and that the rest of the team is basically having to work around me right now. And, well, it's not just at work. At home, my husband says it feels like I'm barely even present anymore. So, yeah, it's definitely affecting things.
When you’re reminded of that work incident, do you ever feel detached from yourself or as if things around you aren’t real?

No, I haven't really felt anything like that. I mean, I get stressed and overwhelmed, but I've never felt like I wasn't real or like I was detached from my own body. Things around me still feel real, just... really hard to deal with right now.
